solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They are a recognised doubles pair

definitions.text: They are a recognised doubles pair

parts.words: They are a recognised doubles pair
parts.note: a doubles pair sounds like two tennis partners, but here the doubles are lookalikes of a person, recognised as near-identical copies

explanation.surface: A well-known tennis doubles partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis setting of the puzzle pushes 'doubles' towards the game; the clue means people who are exact likenesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of uncanny lookalikes are each other's doubles, so they are a recognised pair of identical-seeming people.

clue.text: Do it around the country, first escaping injury from a pet

indicators.note: the words do and it are placed around the country's abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

indicators.note: first indicates the opening letter of the word escaping

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tour the land, getting away first, after being hurt by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound caused by a dog's teeth is the classic hurt inflicted by a household animal.

clue.text: Telephoned after parking to report a crash

indicators.note: the telephoned word comes after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone phones in after parking to say there has been an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a minor collision, especially of a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Removes tax up to a point

indicators.note: up to means placed right next to, so the point follows the tax

parts.note: excise is a duty charged on goods
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Something takes away tax only to a certain degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out, so the verb is a synonym for takes away.

clue.text: The last statement in court proceedings

definitions.text: The last statement in court proceedings

parts.words: The last statement in court proceedings
parts.note: court suggests a law court, but the umpire's call at the end of a tennis match is the final statement made on court

explanation.surface: The closing words in a legal trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpire announces this phrase when a tennis match is won, so it is the final utterance in play on court.

clue.text: A small area that is for relations commonly

parts.note: a nook is a small recess or corner
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A little space set aside for family members.
explanation.definitionFit: This is colloquial slang for sexual intercourse, the 'relations' in their informal sense.

clue.text: Verify this meant without a public institution

indicators.note: this stands for the answer itself: the answer followed by the shortened word makes the institution, so that word is removed from it

parts.note: the Establishment is the ruling institutional order of a country

indicators.note: without tells us the letter a is dropped from the word meant

explanation.surface: Confirm what was intended, with no state body involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'this' as the answer: the answer plus MENT (MEANT 'without a') gives ESTABLISHMENT, so taking MENT from ESTABLISHMENT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to prove or confirm it, a synonym for verify.

clue.text: Former champion has a politician and gunner on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts these pieces within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one is aboard
MP is a Member of Parliament
RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: An ex-titleholder travels with an MP and an artilleryman on his team.
explanation.definitionFit: Pete Sampras won fourteen Grand Slam singles titles, a past tennis champion.

clue.text: Lawyer joins artist to find site of an Indian masterpiece

parts.note: AG is the Attorney General, the government's chief lawyer
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A lawyer and an artist team up to locate a great Indian work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal, India's most famous architectural masterpiece, stands in this city.

clue.text: Period spent in the park bar with four measures

indicators.note: a period spent in the park is time on the common, so the park word comes first

parts.note: a common is public parkland
time means a period

explanation.surface: Time passed in a park, then a pub with four drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' and 'measures' look like a pub and drinks; they are musical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this signature has four crotchet beats to each bar, 4/4.

clue.text: Nothing is impossible shows Swiss champion

indicators.note: shows means the phrase displays the name within its letters, running across word breaks

explanation.surface: A motivational slogan reveals a sports star.
explanation.walkthrough: The slogan reads like a deletion of NOT from 'Nothing'; in fact the name runs straight through notHING IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Martina Hingis, born in Slovakia, played for Switzerland and won five Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Peel a small flower and graze

parts.note: skin and peel both mean the outer layer of fruit
a burn is a small stream in Scotland, and a flower in crosswords is something that flows

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip a little blossom and nibble it.
explanation.definitionFit: A graze is a surface abrasion, the sort of friction injury suffered falling on a court.

clue.text: Newly carved best ivory in so many words.

indicators.note: carved afresh means the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A finely carved ivory piece described at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Using far too many words is wordiness, so 'so many words' describes it.

clue.text: Suffer serious injury to recover from loss of service

definitions.meaning: in tennis, winning the opponent's serve straight after losing your own

explanation.surface: A player gets badly hurt trying to regain lost ground on serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, damaging the spine; in tennis, immediately winning back a lost service game.

clue.text: Back a saint if it feels comfortable

indicators.note: back tells us the saint's letters and the word if are read in reverse

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Support a holy figure if it seems right.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment that is the right size sits comfortably, so it is a synonym for feeling right on the body.

clue.text: Mathmatical(sic) formula editor printed in various colours

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: An editor checks a maths formula in a document printed in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied means patched with two or more colours, like a magpie's plumage.

clue.text: Expert on keys is in a new gym session

indicators.note: the clue gives no clear container word; gym is read as placing the shuffled letters inside a gym's training session

parts.note: PT, physical training, is a gym session

indicators.note: new means the letters of is in a are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A keyboard virtuoso turns up for a fresh workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose clue: nothing properly signals the containment, and the blogger found no indicator either; 'gym session' as a place you are in is the best reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled player of the piano is an expert on its keyboard.

clue.text: Dishonest way of delivering service.

definitions.meaning: a serve struck with the hand below shoulder height

explanation.surface: A shady approach to how something is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both sneaky and, in tennis, a low-armed serve.

clue.text: Go into the last two scenic places with a fever

parts.note: enter means go into

indicators.note: the last two indicates the final pair of letters of scenic

explanation.surface: Visiting beauty spots while feverish.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric fever is another name for typhoid, often shortened to just the adjective.

clue.text: Promising potential not applicable to an aroma

parts.note: a scent is an aroma

explanation.surface: A prospect is judged irrelevant to a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being shows promise and potential for development.

clue.text: The last two lonely fathers about to reveal small growths.

indicators.note: about means the fathers' word goes round the selected letters

parts.note: pops is an informal word for fathers

indicators.note: the last two picks the final pair of letters of lonely

explanation.surface: Two lonely dads are about to disclose minor tumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyps are small benign growths on mucous membranes.

clue.text: Support space where secrets are discussed

parts.note: to back is to support
room means space

explanation.surface: A private area for confidential talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A back room is a private place out of public view, where confidential deals are hatched.

clue.text: Refuse to go round the hospital for wild party

indicators.note: the refuse word is made to go round the hospital letter

parts.note: trash is refuse, rubbish
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Rubbish is taken around the hospital ahead of a raucous do.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British slang for a lively party.

clue.text: Make an excursion with some French to Namibian town

parts.note: a run is a short trip, so to run is to make an excursion
du is French for some, as in du pain

explanation.surface: Taking a trip with some French people to a town in Namibia.
explanation.definitionFit: Rundu is a town in northern Namibia on the Okavango River.

clue.text: Celestial double act

parts.note: a double act suggests a comedy duo, but here it is a pair of suns in the sky orbiting each other

explanation.surface: A heavenly comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Two suns orbiting a common centre form a paired system in the sky, a stellar duo.

clue.text: Refuse to go on railway at Christmas

indicators.note: the refusal goes on, ahead of, the railway letters

parts.note: no is a refusal
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Someone will not take the train at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for the Christmas season, from French.

clue.text: Sorts out the rackets and enters the arena

indicators.note: sorts is read as a verb meaning rearranges, so the following letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A player sorts out the racquets and walks out for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rackets' suggests tennis gear or crime, and 'Sorts out' reads as a phrasal verb; 'Sorts' alone is the anagram signal on OUT THE RACKETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Players walking onto the playing surface to begin a tennis match are entering their arena.
